subject.title: fix: prevent exec approval revocation races

question: After resolving the dirty merge, should OpenClaw accept approval-specific fail-closed stale-lock behavior that can require operator recovery in exchange for preventing unverifiable stale-lock takeover?
rationale: The code safely makes this tradeoff, but the availability and operator-recovery impact is an intentional security policy choice rather than a correctness fact automation should silently approve.

options.title: Keep fail-closed approval locks
options.body: Preserve the current approval-specific mode and document or prove bounded recovery because authorization integrity takes precedence over automatic stale-lock cleanup.

options.title: Design atomic stale recovery first
options.body: Pause landing until the lock owner boundary supports replacement-safe stale recovery without pathname-based unlink races.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed approval locks
recommendation.body: Preserve the current approval-specific mode and document or prove bounded recovery because authorization integrity takes precedence over automatic stale-lock cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the maintained replacement branch and the cross-runtime implementation carrying this explicit security-versus-availability tradeoff.
